correctness.finding: PASS. Every signed sum of 1,2,...,2^a is an odd integer in [-M,M], M=2^{a+1}-1, and the binary expansion gives a bijection between sign vectors and those odd integers. In an equal-sum divisor bipartition of 2^a p, orienting the partition by the nonzero signed p-block sum B>0 makes the equation A=-pB. Therefore unordered partitions are in one-to-one correspondence with positive odd r=B satisfying pr<=M, giving Z=floor((M+p)/(2p)) and the stated exact k-fiber interval. The prime-count formula follows immediately. Double-counting pairs (p,r) by m=pr gives sum_{odd m<=M} omega(m), and prime Mertens with the p=2 term removed gives the submitted B_1-1/2 constant. Independent brute-force divisor-subset enumeration for all admissible odd primes with a<=5 found zero mismatches.

originality.finding: PASS, narrowly scoped. Bhaskara Rao--Peng and Mahanta--Saikia--Yaqubi establish existence criteria for 2^a p and 2^a p^b; current OEIS A083209 records the previously known unique-partition interval (k=1), and A083206 gives only generic subset-sum/coefficient formulas. Current A378652 lists exactly-two cases but does not state the submitted family formula. Targeted searches found no all-k formula, exact interval fibers, limiting prime-parameter law, or omega aggregate identity. The 2008 Clark et al. conference announcement is not independently available as a full text in the searched sources, but later papers summarize its announced existence/Half-Zumkeller results and do not attribute this counting formula to it; that remains a disclosed residual risk.

scientific_value.finding: PASS. The result quantitatively refines a completely classified existence family into an exact count for every member, classifies every fixed partition multiplicity by a prime interval, and derives both a normalized limiting law and an additive-function aggregate identity. The proof is short but yields substantially more information than existence alone.
